correctness.rationale: Under skew forcing, the white set on A evolves using just the neighborhoods of B in A, independently of the colors on B. For a≥3,b≥2 and missing uv, those neighborhoods are A minus {u} for v and A for all other B vertices. With white A-set {u,w1,w2}, both types see at least two whites and u stays white. Pre-filling w1 lets v force w2, then another B vertex forces u. Instead pre-filling u leaves w1,w2 white with two neighbors counted by each B vertex, so w1 stays white. This verifies the claimed exchange obstruction including b=2, and shore swapping handles the other ordering. In the b=2 discussion of the original, the sole B vertex other than v is the unique neighbor of u, not conversely; the stated force and exchange conclusion are valid. For a star plus an isolated vertex the center is always forced, a missing leaf is forced exactly when it is the sole white leaf, and the isolated vertex never changes. This gives the stated direct sum, including the single-leaf case. Empty-set closure fills P4 and is the identity on the two isolated vertices of K1,1-e. Undeleted bicliques have independent corank-one uniform closure on each shore. Inspected the uploaded verifier and its accompanying text without executing it.

The exact all-size classification and reusable three-vertex obstruction turn a general nonclosure phenomenon into a sharp instability statement with fully identified exceptions; this is stronger than one finite counterexample or a computation of ranks.
